readerTitle: The next one can cost almost nothing. Or a whole van.
caseNote: 가상 사례 두 개 (택배 배송업체, 가정 청소 서비스) + 가상 적용 (소프트웨어 회사) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: '하나 더'의 비용은 평균이 아니라, 그 하나가 무엇을 새로 필요하게 만드는지(남는 여유인지, 새 차량·근무·인력인지)로 정해진다.
misconception: 한 건 더 받는 비용은 평균 원가와 같다. 그리고 그 비용은 언제나 일정하다.

factChecks.note: 청소 서비스: 정규 시간 $25 × 3시간 = $75 + 소모품 $6 + 이동비 $9 = $90. 초과근무 1.5배 $37.50 × 3 = $112.50 + $6 + $9 = $127.50. 평균 원가 약 $110은 사무실·보험·차량 리스를 포함한 가정치입니다.
소프트웨어: 지원 인력 3명이 약 1,500명 담당, 현재 1,490명 → 50명 중 10명은 여유 안, 40명은 한도 초과. 서버비 $0.20 × 50 = $10/월. 모두 가상 수치입니다.

cards.title: The next one can cost almost nothing. Or a whole van.
body: A delivery firm and a house-cleaning company get the same request this week: can you fit in a bit more work?
Both owners know their average cost per job. Neither number answers the question.

image.label: A delivery van and a cleaning crew side by side, each with a question mark
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 왼쪽에 소포가 80% 정도 찬 배송 밴, 오른쪽에 청소 도구를 든 청소원 두 명. 두 장면 위에 각각 "+1?" 말풍선. 실제 회사 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Ten more parcels on today's route.
body: Your van does one route a day. The driver, fuel and van cost $200 a run. Loading and scanning add $0.50 per parcel. It holds 100 parcels. Today it carries 80, so each parcel costs $3.00 on average.
A shop asks you to add 10 parcels to today's route. What do those 10 parcels add to your costs?

options.feedback: The average includes the $200 run, which you pay whether you carry 80 parcels or 90. Using it here overstates the cost six times.

options.text: About $5: just the loading and scanning
options.feedback: Right. The van is going anyway and has room, so only the handling is new. Next card shows what happens when the van fills up.

options.text: Split the $200 across all 90 parcels and use that
options.feedback: That gives a new average of about $2.72. It describes the whole day, not what the 10 extra parcels add.

cards.title: Same van, three very different numbers.

breakdown.label: Parcels 81 to 100
breakdown.detail: Just handling. The van has room

breakdown.label: Parcel 101
breakdown.detail: The van is full. It needs a second run

cards.callout: Now the shop wants 30 parcels. Twenty fit for $10. The last 10 need a second run for $205. The order adds **$215**, almost all from the last ten.

cards.title: Marginal cost
body: **Marginal cost** is how much your total cost goes up when you make or deliver one more unit.
It is not the average. The average spreads all your costs across everything you did. Marginal cost asks only: *what changes if I say yes to this one?*
For the van, the answer swings from 50 cents to $200, depending on whether there is room left.

image.label: Staircase chart: flat steps with one tall jump when the van fills
image.brief: 계단형 그래프. 가로축 "Parcels", 세로축 "Total cost". 0~100개 구간은 완만하게 오르다가 101번째에서 큰 계단으로 뛰어오름. 계단 부분에 "Second van run" 라벨, 완만한 구간에 "$0.50 each" 라벨.

cards.title: A cleaning company sees a different pattern.
body: Your cleaners earn $25 an hour. A typical job takes 3 hours, plus $6 of supplies and $9 of travel. One more job costs $90. With office, insurance and van leases spread in, your average is about $110.
In a full week, the extra job goes to someone on overtime at time and a half. Now it costs $127.50, *more* than the average.

groups.label: Cost of one more cleaning job

cards.title: Ask what the next one triggers.
body: In the van business, most of the cost sits in the run. Extra parcels ride almost free until the van is full. Then one parcel costs a whole trip.
In the cleaning business, most of the cost is people's time, which grows with every job. Marginal cost stays close to the average, then **climbs when the team is stretched**.
Either way, look for the next step: a full van, a full schedule, a new hire, a second shift.

image.label: Two lines: one flat with a big jump, one steady then rising
image.brief: 두 개의 작은 그래프를 나란히 배치. 왼쪽 "Delivery": 거의 평평하다가 한 번 크게 뛰는 선. 오른쪽 "Cleaning": 일정하게 오르다가 끝부분에서 가팔라지는 선. 각 그래프에 "Next step" 화살표 표시.

cards.title: Cheap extras still have to pay for the base.
body: If you price every parcel at 50 cents, nobody pays for the van. Marginal cost tells you what a single yes costs. It doesn't tell you what prices keep the business alive.
Some marginal costs also show up late. A crew on overtime every week gets tired, makes mistakes and quits. Count those costs once the extra work becomes the normal work.

cards.title: Now it's a software company.
body: Your app costs about $0.20 per customer each month in servers. Your three support staff can handle about 1,500 customers, and you have 1,490.
A partner offers to bring in 50 new customers next month. What will they really cost to serve?

options.text: About $10 a month, just the servers
options.feedback: True for the first 10. The other 40 push past what support can handle, so the real cost includes a step you haven't counted.

options.text: Servers plus a fourth support hire, unless you can cut support needs first
options.feedback: This finds the step. Now you can choose: hire, add self-serve help, or shape the deal so it covers the extra person.

options.text: Total monthly costs divided by customers, times 50
options.feedback: It gives a rough figure but hides the jump. The first 10 cost almost nothing; the next 40 may cost a salary.

cards.title: Ask what the next one costs, not what the average one costs.
body: Marginal cost can be near zero or huge. It depends on whether you have room, or need a new van, shift or person.
**Try it today:** find your next step. How many more orders, jobs or customers can you take before you must add a big new cost?
